senses.sense_definition: The act, process, or state of going beyond usual or physical limits.

examples.text: Great works of art often achieve a sense of <w>transcendence</w> that speaks to people across different eras.
Through deep meditation, she experienced a profound moment of personal <w>transcendence</w>.

senses.sense_definition: The state of existing independently of and beyond the physical world or human understanding, especially of a deity.

examples.text: The philosopher discussed divine <w>transcendence</w> in contrast to the idea that God is within all things.
Many traditional religions emphasize both the <w>transcendence</w> and the closeness of their creator.

senses.sense_definition: The state of being beyond the range of ordinary human perception or experience.

examples.text: The mystic spoke of the complete <w>transcendence</w> of ordinary consciousness during his visions.
Certain psychological experiences challenge our understanding of reality by offering a taste of perceptual <w>transcendence</w>.

senses.sense_definition: Superior excellence; the quality of being exceptionally distinguished or preeminent.

examples.text: The sheer <w>transcendence</w> of her musical talent amazed every critic in the concert hall.
His technical performance was admired for its undisputed <w>transcendence</w> over all competitors.

senses.sense_definition: The mathematical property of being a transcendental number, not root of any non-zero polynomial with rational coefficients.

examples.text: The mathematician published an elegant proof establishing the <w>transcendence</w> of the constant.
Mathematicians celebrated when the <w>transcendence</w> of pi was finally demonstrated in the nineteenth century.
